d: Part of the rebuilt Milan, in the vicinity of the walls. From one part of the city there are the Militi piacantini and some Centurie of Verona, Brescia, Novara and Vercelli: the district is crowded of Popolo, like the above veronas, from which hang colorful tapestries and julive garlande: a universal cry of exultation, a prolonged batter of palm trees, and a nembo of flowers falling from above on the teams attests the festive welcomes to them. Arrigo is among the Verona warriors.
Rolando, other Milanese duci, and sayings.
The Consuls with Séguito, and sayings.
Site shaded by groups of trees near the water-filled ditches, which surround the walls: they veggonsi tower in the bottom.
Marcovaldo, and said.
Imelda, and sayings.
Rolando, Arrigo, and sayings.
An Herald, and sayings.
Magnificent hall in the town hall of Como: verons closed in the bottom. Gradually they are assembled Dukes and Magistrates.
The Podestà, and sayings.
Rolando and Arrigo are introduced to a nod of the Podestà.
Federico, and sayings.

Underground times in the temple of St Ambrose scattered of recent tombs: stepd at the bottom for which you descend; a dim lamp throws around some uncertain ray. The Knights of death gradually descend, and in silence: each of them carries a gun-necked ciarp, on which he placed the head of a human skeleton.
Arrigo, and sayings.
Apartments in the castle of Rolando. Lida, and Imelda.
Rolando, and said.
I'm on my way.
Marcovaldo, that's it.
A room on the top of the tower: iron door on one side, at the bottom verona that responds on the ditches of the walls. The brunette Arrigo ciarp hangs from the armpits of a seat. Arrigo.
Lida, that's it.
Rolando, that's it.
Lida, and sayings.

Piazza di Milano where there is a temple vestibule. The embellished women, the old trembles and the innocent children are part in the vestibule and part on the way: Lida there is also with Imelda, and all genuflexs hear in religious recollection the salmodies that start from the inside.
Second consul and senators, followed by large cast of Citizens, and sayings.
Arrigo mortally wounded, and supported by some Knights of death: more Milanese dukes follow him, among them Rolando, who advances silent and chino head. The above.
The first console followed by a long section of Armati, and the triumphal chariot.
